ranking.note: Raised to match #36105: both are defects that make the shipped bitcoin wrapper unusable or silently wrong on real installs
Lowered to sit with #31888: both are narrow fixes to the same niche linearize contrib script, which the category ranks low regardless
Lowered: internal clang-tidy refactor aid with no user-facing payoff, and the author prefers abandoning the approach

inconsistencies: #36105 and #36190 form a chain: #36190 only adds Windows functional tests on top of the ExecVp fix in #36105; review #36105 first, #36190 is the regression-test follow-up.

#36157 and #31888 both patch contrib/linearize/linearize-data.py for different defects (infinite loop on zero padding vs. output truncation/stale data); they should be banded together and reviewed together to avoid conflicting rewrites of the same file — #36157 first, as it is a one-line fix with a reproduction while #31888 has been stalled for months.

#35608 and #35809 both modify the deterministic-fuzz-coverage tool; #35608 (skip redundant llvm-cov rendering) gives the larger benefit and should be reviewed first, with #35809 (optional coverage_check argument) rebased on it.
#35903 may be moot: a reviewer asked whether #35958 makes the non-printable msgtype condition unreachable; that question should be resolved before spending review time here.

#19460 sits on the multiprocess branch (#10102/#29409) and is the base of #19461, so its value is conditional on that chain landing; #27409 builds on already-merged #27302 and is independently reviewable.
result.notes: The category has one clear security item (#36293) and two genuine tool defects in the bitcoin wrapper; everything else is developer-productivity tooling or niche contrib scripts, so the bulk correctly sits in P3 with the narrow contrib fixes in P4.
